# Ablation on SYNTHETIC data (smoke test)

**These numbers come from synthetic EEG generated by `seizure_gnn.data.SyntheticEEG`. They show that the pipeline runs end to end and that each model can learn a deliberately learnable toy task. They are not research results and are not comparable to the poster's mid-70% accuracy, which was measured on a real EEG dataset with the original code.**

Generated by `python scripts/run_ablation.py` (CPU, 88 s).

Setup: 12 synthetic recordings of 120 s, 16 channels at 128 Hz, 2 seizures each, effect_strength=0.5; 2 s windows with 1 s stride; edges = 0.5 |Pearson| + 0.5 normalized MI, top-4 neighbors; sequences of T=6 windows labeled by window t+1 (next-window prediction); split by recording 60/20/20; 5 DGI epochs, 10 supervised epochs, best epoch chosen by validation AUC. Mean ± std over seeds [0, 1, 2] (each seed regenerates the data and the split).

| Model | Accuracy | F1 | ROC AUC |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fusion (DGI-pretrained GCN + TCN) | 0.975 ± 0.009 | 0.959 ± 0.019 | 0.994 ± 0.003 |
| Fusion without DGI pretraining | 0.963 ± 0.009 | 0.941 ± 0.024 | 0.993 ± 0.002 |
| SpatialOnly (GCN on last window) | 0.945 ± 0.031 | 0.914 ± 0.043 | 0.990 ± 0.006 |
| TemporalOnly (TCN on features, no graph) | 0.948 ± 0.024 | 0.922 ± 0.034 | 0.991 ± 0.002 |

## How to read this

* Every model is near the ceiling, because the synthetic seizures (amplitude jump plus a shared 3-8 Hz rhythm) are easy to see. The gaps between rows are mostly within one or two standard deviations over only three seeds, so this table does **not** show that fusion beats the baselines. Ranking the models needs real EEG.
* Accuracy and F1 use a fixed 0.5 threshold while the checkpoint is picked by validation AUC, and the loss is class-weighted, so a model can rank windows well (high AUC) yet be poorly calibrated at 0.5. In a harder run (`--effect-strength 0.2`, seed 0) the DGI fusion model had AUC 0.985 but accuracy 0.51 for this reason. Tuning the threshold on validation data is a planned improvement.
